title: Constructing number systems: integers, rationals, and real numbers

based_on.title: Set Theory: An Open Introduction
based_on.pages: 73–88 (§§6.1–6.6, quotient constructions and Dedekind cuts; online revision July 2026)

summary: Quotients supply integers and rationals; cuts fill rational gaps to give the complete real field.
abstract: Natural numbers cannot solve every equation: subtraction leads to negative integers, and division by nonzero numbers leads to rational fractions. These extensions can be built from pairs of existing numbers, identifying pairs that describe the same value. The rational numbers still leave gaps, including the missing square root of two. A Dedekind cut records the rational numbers on the lower side of such a gap, providing a way to construct the real numbers from the rationals. These cuts satisfy the usual arithmetic and the least-upper-bound property: every nonempty collection bounded above has a smallest upper bound.
